- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap peak forecast at 2–3% below true peak or adjust downward 1–2 days after spike.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) and model is rising, reduce forecast slope; model often overreacts to negative sentiment, leading to premature recovery.
- Mean reversion bias: if model is above 10% above recent 5-day average, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period price action (last 5–7 days); apply 1–2% upward adjustment for final 5–7 days if sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– cycles, model tends to lag in direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend 1–2 days ahead, not 3–5 days behind.
